environment: Production API, Tempo 2.10.3, Grafana 13.0.2; Windows development host
scenario: Correlate independent authenticated API traces by verified account and session; group requests into navigable sessions in Grafana.

observations: Focused tests were written first and failed before implementation.
Require and Optional attach verified user.id and a domain-separated session.id without exporting the session token or digest.
Tests cover stable/distinct session identifiers, anonymous/zero-digest cases, failed authentication and forged identity headers.
Focused Go tests, affected-package go vet and the full local go test -count=1 ./... command passed. CI also passed the PostgreSQL-backed backend gate.

results.check: Dashboard contracts and real Tempo responses
observations: All five Python dashboard tests passed; the workflow validation script passed.
All 11 dashboard TraceQL queries returned HTTP 200 from deployed Tempo.
Tempo returned unscoped response keys user.id and session.id; Grafana groupBy uses these exact keys while TraceQL uses span.user.id and span.session.id.
Native service filters include web, android, ios, windows and macos. Background workers are separated; WebSocket lifetime is excluded from slow HTTP requests.
Updated the existing boohtacord-traces dashboard and verified the saved view in the authenticated browser.
13 independent request traces grouped into one session row: mean duration 5.18 ms, maximum 25.2 ms.
Clicking the session set both user and session filters; the request timeline exposed valid trace/span links.
A subsequent private Tempo check returned 22 correlated request traces and confirmed expected attribute names without printing identifier values.
Both implementation commits were integrated into GitHub master.
Production deployment succeeded for the final dashboard revision.
CI backend, frontend, contracts and container publication passed for that revision.

limits: Session aggregates describe a bounded search sample: at most 500 traces and 50 matching spans per trace, not exact total traffic.
Old traces cannot acquire user/session attributes retroactively and remain available in diagnostics.
Client-only traces without a correlated API span remain in diagnostics; delayed client batches are not attributed to the current login.
No new live voice or screen-sharing action was exercised after this rollout; the proof covers authenticated HTTP grouping, query validity and navigation.
